clue.text: Art to be found in certain puzzles — and in the other across solutions

definitions.text: Art to be found in certain puzzles — and in the other across solutions

parts.words: Art to be found in certain puzzles — and in the other across solutions
parts.note: children's puzzle pages print drawings with objects concealed in them, and every other across answer here conceals a film title

explanation.surface: A puzzle-page feature that this very crossword also contains.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is also the theme: each other across answer hides a film, as ALI in ITALIC, ARGO in CARGOS, THOR in AUTHORED, EMMA in LEMMAS, MASH in SMASHHIT, ET in PINETREE and HELP in WHELPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzle books feature drawings in which objects are concealed for the reader to spot; here 'pictures' also means movies.

clue.text: Clips of omissions from a hippie classic?

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical of the hippie movement
cuts are parts left out of a film or show

explanation.surface: Asking about the scenes cut from a famous musical about hippies.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a trim of the hair, so clips are trims given by a barber.

clue.text: Who, for example, is ahead of a film star princess in frantic contest?

indicators.note: puts the doctor's letters before what follows, in reading order

parts.note: Doctor Who is an example of a doctor, abbreviated DR
Grace Kelly, the film star who became Princess of Monaco

explanation.surface: Imagining Doctor Who racing ahead of a Hollywood princess in some wild competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is a long-running British TV science-fiction series.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag race is a short, furious sprint between cars from a standing start, a frenzied competition.

clue.text: One nasty guy cutting blockbuster in pieces

indicators.note: the nasty guy and the one slice into the middle of the blockbuster

parts.note: an epic is a big, lavish film
I is the Roman numeral one
sod is British slang for an unpleasant man

explanation.surface: A villain hacking a blockbuster film to bits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something episodic comes in separate instalments or episodes rather than one continuous whole.

clue.text: See 1
I study old cinema, initially with ultimate critic

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of cinema

parts.note: ultimate means last

explanation.surface: A film critic describing studying old cinema with an eye on the final word.
explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast attacks cherished beliefs and institutions, a harsh critic of the established order.

clue.text: Dress protecting male and female in horror film

indicators.note: the dress wraps round the male and the female, keeping them inside

parts.note: to tog is to dress (tog up)
he is a male

explanation.surface: A costume shielding a man and a woman in a scary movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fog is John Carpenter's 1980 supernatural chiller about ghosts emerging from a sea mist.

clue.text: Give a detailed account of story in trailer that's abbreviated and modified

definitions.text: Give a detailed account of story

indicators.note: the remaining letters are altered into a new order
shortened, so trailer loses its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of trailer, cut off

explanation.surface: Telling a story from a film trailer that has been cut down and changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abbreviated' drops the final R to leave TRAILE, and 'modified' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail a story is to recount or relate it in full, an older sense of the word beside selling.

clue.text: Child was portrayed by this actress when about 60

definitions.text: Child was portrayed by this actress when about 60

parts.words: Child was portrayed by this actress when about 60
parts.note: the chef Julia Child was played in Julie & Julia (2009) by an actress born in 1949

explanation.walkthrough: 'Child' looks like a youngster, which makes a 60-year-old actress absurd; it is Julia Child, the American TV cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep played the celebrity cook Julia Child in the 2009 film Julie & Julia, at the age of sixty.

clue.text: Inclined to show stress in hospital, I confess

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, running across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of hospital through I into the start of confess

explanation.surface: A patient admitting to feeling stressed while in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides the film ALI, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Italic type slants to the right and is used to show emphasis in print.

clue.text: Funny guy's agreement secured by another

indicators.note: the agreement is held inside the other funny man

parts.note: another funny guy, a jester
OK signals agreement

explanation.surface: A comedian's deal clinched by a second comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points back to the definition: a second funny guy, the jester. The answer hides KES, Ken Loach's film.
explanation.definitionFit: A jokester is someone who tells jokes, a comic or wag.

clue.text: Things to take on board or move into road transport

indicators.note: the move goes inside the road vehicles

parts.note: cars are road vehicles
to go is to move

explanation.surface: Choosing between loading goods aboard or shifting them onto lorries.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides ARGO, the 2012 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargoes are goods loaded onto a ship or plane to be carried.

clue.text: It's rocky as result of drop in share

definitions.note: the definition says what the answer is: a kind of rock

indicators.note: the drop goes inside the share

parts.note: to dole is to share out, and a dole is a portion
to omit is to drop or leave out

explanation.surface: A shaky market explained by a fall in share prices.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolomite is a carbonate mineral and sedimentary rock, which gave the Dolomite mountains their name.

clue.text: Vehicle followed by second in French comedy, treat with superficial sweetness

indicators.note: the car comes first, the film after it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: the second goes inside the film title

parts.note: Amélie (2001) is a French romantic comedy

explanation.surface: Seeing a car drive by in a French film, then sugar-coating something.
explanation.definitionFit: To caramelise is to coat with melted sugar; figuratively, to make something look sweeter than it is.

clue.text: Total including century after start of play, following plan

indicators.note: the total holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a tally is a running total

indicators.note: the century comes after the start of play

parts.note: Act I is the opening act of a play
C is the abbreviation for a century, or Roman 100

explanation.surface: A scorer adding up a century early in the match, according to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of play' is not the letter P but the play's first act, ACT I. 'century' and 'play' suggest cricket, where a century is 100 runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting tactically means doing things according to a planned strategy.

clue.text: Giddy fame secured by star from the silent era that one tries to land?

indicators.note: the reworked fame is held inside the star's name

parts.note: Lillian Gish was a leading actress of silent films

indicators.note: giddy means dizzy and whirling, so the letters of fame spin round

explanation.surface: Giddy fame captured by an old silent-film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Game fish are sporting fish such as marlin or salmon that anglers try to hook and reel in.

clue.text: One's removed from a blue film, oddly culpable

indicators.note: the one is taken out of the fodder before it is rearranged
in an odd, strange way, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone guiltily cutting a single scene from a smutty film.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of A BLUE FILM, then 'oddly' rearranges the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameful means deserving blame, a synonym of guilty or blameworthy.

clue.text: Nonsense about English director cutting one line in scene of The Singing Nun

indicators.note: the nonsense goes around the director's shortened name

parts.note: BS is the abbreviation for bullshit, nonsense

indicators.note: the director's name loses one of its letters

parts.note: Ken Russell, the English film director
L is the abbreviation for line; only one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: Complaining about a director's edits to a film about a singing nun.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Russell's surname has two Ls, and 'one line' takes away only one of them. BS is coarse slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Singing Nun, Jeannine Deckers, was a Belgian nun from a convent near the Belgian capital, the setting of the 1966 film about her.

clue.text: Jazz pianist's arrangement of Waterfalls

indicators.note: in music an arrangement reworks a piece, and here the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A jazz musician's version of a tune called Waterfalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Waller was a celebrated American stride pianist and composer of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Musical animated movie — saucy stuff

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
Up is the 2009 Pixar animated film

explanation.surface: Reviewing a musical cartoon film that turns out to be rather racy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' looks like risqué, but it means made of sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is an American variant spelling of ketchup, the tomato sauce.

clue.text: Sound of music coming from orchestra inside

indicators.note: coming from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Music heard drifting out of a concert hall where an orchestra plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound of music' recalls the film musical, but here it simply defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a passage or snatch of melody, as in 'the strains of a waltz'.

clue.text: Screwball comedy that needs work put into it

indicators.note: the work is placed inside the word that

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A madcap comedy that needs more effort put into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Hat is the 1935 Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers musical, a screwball romantic comedy of mistaken identity.

clue.text: Wrote as American essayist, having moved gold to front, followed by diamonds

indicators.note: the diamonds come after the rest
the gold is shifted from its place in the essayist's name
the gold goes to the front of the name

parts.note: Henry David Thoreau, author of Walden
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Writing like Thoreau after a prospector's move of gold and diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: The final AU of THOREAU goes to the front, giving AUTHORE, then D. The answer hides THOR.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a work is to write it, so authored is a synonym of composed or penned.

clue.text: They help with proof in problem mastery

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, across the gap

parts.note: the letters run from the end of problem into the start of mastery

explanation.surface: Aids to proving something buried in a mastery of problems.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides EMMA, the Jane Austen adaptation.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics, lemmas are subsidiary theorems proved first to help establish a main result.

clue.text: Outstanding success in strike after strike

parts.note: to smash is to strike hard
to hit is to strike

explanation.surface: A great triumph built from one blow after another.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer hides MASH, the Korean War comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a hugely popular show, song or film.

clue.text: Cobblers can make a lot of money covering pair of feet

indicators.note: the money wraps around the pair of feet

parts.note: a pile is a fortune
F stands for foot, so FF is two feet

explanation.surface: Shoe repairers earning a fortune by covering people's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' looks like shoemakers, but it is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are informal British terms for rubbish or nonsense talk.

clue.text: Entire EP remixed — it's an evergreen

indicators.note: a remix rearranges a recording, and here it rearranges the letters

explanation.surface: A whole extended-play record remixed into a timeless classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evergreen' suggests a perennial song, but here it is a tree. The answer hides ET.
explanation.definitionFit: Pines are conifers that keep their needles all year, a classic example of an evergreen.

clue.text: Page in Welsh converted for young English setters, say

indicators.note: turned into something different, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: Welsh text with a page translated into English for some setters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' looks like crossword setters; it is the dog breed. The answer hides HELP!, the Beatles film.
explanation.definitionFit: Whelps are puppies, and English setters are a breed of gun dog.
